body.statement: There are constants \(C<\infty\) and \(n_0\), depending only on \(\alpha\) and the fixed indices \(B_A,B_Y,\beta,R_f,R_q,\kappa,q_e,M_e,\nu_0,c_0,p_{\min},|\mathcal X|\), such that the deterministic construction \(\mathfrak H^{\mathrm{up}}\) yields jointly sample-and-index measurable finite endpoints with \(L_n(a)\le U_n(a)\) for every \(a\in I\) almost surely, \(\mathcal C_n\in\mathfrak B_{n,\alpha}\), and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}}[W_n]\le Cr_n\) for every \(n\ge n_0\). Coverage follows on \(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\). On every realized regular-count sample \(\min_xn_x\ge np_{\min}/2\), the width is at most \(Cr_n\) regardless of coverage-event failure; clipping bounds it by \(2B_Y\) on the exponentially rare count failure. The multinomial coordinate contributes \(O([\log(|\mathcal X|/\alpha)/n]^{1/2})=o(r_n)\) to the diameter.
body.justification: The statement turns blind analytic identification into uniform whole-curve inference at a quantitative width.
body.gap: Kato and Sasaki use an auxiliary-error or symmetric repeated-measurement design with conventional deconvolution, while Babii treats a fixed linear inverse operator; neither controls joint cell-mass profiling, this blind asymmetric bilinear factorization, and the causal quotient.
body.consumer: It supplies whole-curve uncertainty for the Melaku--Shi (2026) NHANES two-recall diet--mortality mvGPS analysis rather than pointwise intervals.

obligation.what_is_open: Uniform causal coverage and the expected-width bound await the pointwise causal bridge, feasible embedding, and deterministic analytic stability modulus.
obligation.obstruction: The theorem consumes both the currently false pointwise ADRF identification statement and the unresolved load-bearing parts of \(\mathrm{lem{:}analytic\text{-}sieve\text{-}stability}\). Proving only the concentration event cannot bound the profile diameter.
obligation.attempted: I completed the reduction from those missing ingredients to coverage and expected width, including the regular-count/failure split and the exact exponentially small remainder.
obligation.partial_result:
If the unresolved embedding and deterministic stability assertions in \(\mathrm{lem{:}analytic\text{-}sieve\text{-}stability}\) hold and the pointwise causal bridge is added, the remainder of the upper theorem is complete.  On \(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\), a feasible approximating tuple \(\bar\theta\) with \(\|\mu_{\bar\theta}-\mu\|_\infty\le b_{\mu,n}\) implies \(L_n\le\mu\le U_n\) pointwise by the endpoint definitions.  On the regular-count event, deterministic feasible-set diameter plus the two endpoint inflations is \(O(r_n)\), since \(b_{\mu,n}=O(K_n^{1/2-\beta})\) and \(\sqrt{\lambda_n/n}=o(r_n)\).  On count failure, clipping gives \(W_n\le2B_Y\), while \(\mathrm{lem{:}mass\text{-}confidence}\) gives probability at most \(|\mathcal X|e^{-np_{\min}/8}\).  Therefore
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M}E_PW_n
 \le Cr_n+2B_Y|\mathcal X|e^{-np_{\min}/8}
 =O(r_n).
\]
Thus no additional probabilistic argument is missing; the analytic inverse modulus, feasible embedding, and pointwise causal bridge are the exact blockers.
